why: B moved materially more traffic (the hard-coded reviewer and o1 snapshots mapped so the review stage actually routes, 12 verified sites vs 6) and its system-level claims hold up better: it does the cost math that shows splitting the n=5 ensemble would cost 2-3x for no quality gain, separates OpenAI's automatic prefix caching (~-48% on a repeat, which it measured) from a real lever, and then proposes Claude cache_control where caching is not automatic with token-level evidence (-90% on the repeated prefix). A's one genuinely better idea — the reviewer on gpt-5.4-mini at Flex, -82% measured, the only use of tier-as-priority in either report — does not offset that its headline cache saving looks like the automatic caching B identified, that its ensemble fix would raise spend, and that it left the reviewer on OpenAI as a 'decision' while reporting near-complete coverage.
A_best: The reviewer-on-gpt-5.4-mini-at-Flex branch: correct read that nothing in this pipeline waits on a user, so the background tier is free money, with a measured -82% per review call — the only real use of tier as priority in either submission.
B_best: Verified honesty about the default path: it read litellm 1.81.10 and showed that install_litellm only reaches the OpenAI provider, so aider on the default claude-3-5-sonnet does not route, and said so plainly rather than letting 'aider is on Router' stand — paired with the standalone temperature-TypeError quick win that is the precondition for the Claude model and caching branches.
A_worst: Two of its six improvements rest on shaky numbers or economics — the -48% 'prompt cache keys' gain is almost certainly OpenAI's automatic prefix caching (B measured the same -48% with no key change), and ensemble-without-n would route five calls at roughly 2-3x the input cost of the n=5 call it replaces, a tradeoff it mentions but never prices.
B_worst: It put a behaviour change in the migration branch itself — mapping the reviewer's pinned May-2024 gpt-4o to the August snapshot, which shifts the review scores this app exists to produce — right after arguing elsewhere that a silently different reviewer model corrupts that measurement; it should have been an approvable branch like A treated it.
